name: INSTATIQ P1 (Progress One)
summary: Mobile 3D concrete printer with a 26 m automatically controlled boom that prints load-bearing walls on site from standard ready-mix concrete. Made by INSTATIQ, a Putzmeister spin-off near Stuttgart, and used on German and Austrian building sites.

germany.statusNote: Offered in Germany by the Stuttgart maker as a printing service: INSTATIQ works as technology partner for the printing, helps integrate it into existing building processes or delivers the complete automated shell; first consultation on request. Printing services are also sold through NELCON, a joint venture of STRABAG and INSTATIQ. No machine sale or price is shown on the pages read.

sellers.name: INSTATIQ GmbH
sellers.note: Schelmenwasenstraße 37, 70567 Stuttgart. Sells printing work as a service (technology partner, process integration or full automated shell), not a listed machine sale. Phone number as printed on the maker's news pages (0711 93313030).

specs.label: Boom reach
specs.quote: der Reichweite unseres Roboters von bis zu 26 Metern

specs.label: Wall thickness
specs.quote: DRUCKBREITE – Wandstärken von 8 bis 40 cm, echte Massivbauweise

specs.label: Concrete output
specs.quote: a maximum output of 2.5 cubic meters per hour

specs.label: Printed wall height
specs.conditions: up to 7 m at the Neubulach supermarket; up to 3 m per storey at Metzingen

specs.label: Material
specs.value: standard ready-mix concrete, no special mortar
specs.quote: TRANSPORTBETON – Drucken mit klassischem Beton, kein Spezialmörtel

notes: The arm is a 26 m automatically controlled boom with a print head; the maker compares it with a mobile concrete pump.
How the machine is carried and moved between sites (truck or other carrier) is not described on the pages read; wheels and tracks are left false.
Prints solid load-bearing walls, not formwork, from concrete delivered by a normal mixer truck.
The printer is repositioned between storeys on multi-storey jobs (Weerberg).

evidence.task: Printed the load-bearing walls of the top floor of a four-storey apartment building directly on site in four days
evidence.where: GWG Reutlingen housing, Metzingen-Neugreuth, Germany – ZÜBLIN
evidence.note: The projects page later says the walls of the top two storeys were printed.

evidence.task: Printed more than 1,300 m² of wall with walls up to 7 m high for a supermarket; two P1 printers worked in parallel in some phases
evidence.where: Neubulach, Germany – NELCON, Heidelberg Materials, Köhler Bauunternehmung Wildberg

evidence.task: Printing about 890 m² of walls in two thicknesses (17.5 and 24 cm) for an office and warehouse building
Printing about 682 m² of load-bearing walls from about 179 m³ of concrete for a four-storey headquarters building
evidence.where: Weerberg, Tyrol, Austria – NELCON and STRABAG
evidence.note: Printing planned to finish in January 2027, building in March 2027.
